title: Executive read: what this docket could change
intro: Vahana Labs interpretation of the public comments, written for product, strategy and operating leaders. It is editorial, not a commenter position, and every theme links to the questions it draws on.

takeaways.title: Evidence burden and market structure
takeaways.text: Commenters back evidence that scales with risk, but proportionality only helps if sponsors can predict the evidence bar before they design a program. Where that bar cannot be anticipated, development cost, capital requirements, and time to market stay uncertain, and a uniform evidence floor could make lower-value informational use cases uneconomic and favor incumbents.

takeaways.title: The product boundary expands
takeaways.text: For multi-turn and agentic systems, the comments treat the regulated product as more than the model. Permission architecture, tool interfaces, logging, rollback controls, human-intervention design, and a declared envelope of permitted behavior may all become part of what is evaluated, which makes intended-use boundaries an early product decision rather than a labeling exercise.

takeaways.title: Postmarket monitoring becomes an operating model
takeaways.text: Commenters do not question postmarket monitoring. They ask for a risk-scaled cadence, defined triggers for reassessment, and a named owner for residual risk. If re-benchmarking, telemetry, clinician review, and event-triggered requalification become expected, they turn into recurring costs and shared responsibilities between vendors and deploying organizations, defined in contracts and implementation plans rather than regulatory files alone.

takeaways.title: Foundation-model dependence is supplier risk
takeaways.text: Commenters treat upstream model change as a problem that contractual notice alone cannot solve, pairing notice rights with version pinning, validation gates, change detection, and rollback. That makes base-model selection an architecture and financing decision. It shapes validation cost, update velocity, switching costs, and diligence, and one submission notes that smaller manufacturers may lack the leverage to obtain notice at all.

takeaways.title: Deployment assurance may be the differentiator
takeaways.text: A lighter FDA pathway does not necessarily mean a lighter buyer review. Health systems may still ask how evidence maps to their population, workflow, and users. The comments point toward an advantage for companies that can repeatedly demonstrate safe deployment across sites, workflows, populations, and upstream model changes, not only strong model performance.
